items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the general business law, in relation to the secure choice
savings program and participating individuals
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8654

SPONSOR: SAVINO
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the general business law, in relation to the secure
choice savings program and participating individuals

 
PURPOSE:

To allow "participating individuals" defined as any individual who
enrolls in the program independent of a employments relationship with an
eligible employer, maintains and account in the program, and is not a
participating employee.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Article 43 of the General Business Law - The New York State Secure
Choice Savings Program to allow participating individuals to participate
in the program.

"Participating Individuals":

*any individual who enrolls in the program independent of a employments
relationship with an eligible employer, maintains and account in the
program, and is not a participating employee;

*who is at least eighteen years of age and has New York taxable income
within the calendar year.

The Secure Choice Board shall:

*consider the ability for participating individuals to select their
contribution level which may be expressed as a set dollar amount upon
enrollment, the frequency of such contributions, the ability to make
such contributions by direct deposit, ability to select investment
options, and the termination process;

*facilitate the development of educational materials for participating
individuals; and,

*design and make publicly available informational materials which shall
include background information on the program and how to participate as
a participating individual, including but not limited to, information on
the benefits and risks associated with making contributions to the
program, the process for making contributions, the contribution levels
they may contribute, the process for withdrawal of retirement savings,
and the process for selecting beneficiaries.

 
EXISTING LAW:

Article 43 of the General Business Law - The New York State Secure
Choice Savings Program

 
JUSTIFICATION:

There are well over 200,000 freelancers in New York, representing
diverse specialties such as graphic design, contracting, entrepreneurs,

and moonlighters. In addition, women represent a majority of this work-
force.

One of the major difficulties independent workers face is the ability to
save for retirement. Recent surveys found that over 75% of freelancers
said saving for retirement was a top concern. In addition, more than 52%
of those surveyed in New York City said they did not feel on track for
retirement. Furthermore, 42% of non-traditional workers do not have a
defined benefit (401k or similar) plan, compared to 65% of the total
labor force.

A Brookings report found that only 30% of the lowest paid workers have
access to employer-sponsored retirement plans. Additionally, Federal
Reserve data shows that 36% of working Black households have no money
saved for retirement. The figure is 39% for Hispanics and 21% for white
households.

New York took an important step to help New Yorkers save for retirement
by creating the Secure Choice program that required employers who did
not offer their employees a retirement plan to enroll employees in New
York's state-run savings plan. This legislation will build off that step
and expand the program to include the self-employed helping even more
working New Yorkers save for retirement.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2022 Session - new bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately and enrollment of participating individuals shall begin no
later than December thirty-first, two thousand twenty-three.
